explanation: N1858+ fires at the determiner-bound head noun that names a specific-but-unnamed body of prior research findings or records - 'some/various/several/multiple/certain/many/previous/recent/earlier/existing/the same/one ... studies, study, reports, results, data, work, literature, trials, experiments, papers, findings, surveys' (more weakly 'cases') - the point where expository prose finishes citing that prior body of work just before saying what it shows. The level is set by the surrounding research register more than by the noun alone: 'Several studies have shown ...' reads 3.4 after a methods sentence but 1.5 after a news sentence, bare 'Studies have shown ...' with no determiner reads 0.5, 'Some studies are on the shelf' still reads 2.6, while ordinary plurals and non-research heads ('some apples', 'several students', 'previous owners', 'her work') read at or near baseline.
